topic: DP-3T: The Privacy-Preserving Architecture of Digital Contact Tracing
target_audience: University students (Computer Science, Data Privacy, or Cybersecurity)

sections.title: Introduction: The Privacy Paradox
lecture_lines: Digital contact tracing helps stop virus spread quickly.
Centralized systems risk creating a mass surveillance state.
DP-3T ensures notification without revealing individual identities.
animations: Show Alice (#58D68D) and Bob (#5DADE2) with a red virus (#E74C3C) icon appearing.
A central 'Big Brother' eye icon is canceled by a red 'X' (#C0392B).
Alice and Bob's phones glow, and text 'Privacy Preserved' (#F1C40F) appears.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Cryptographic Hash Functions & BLE
lecture_lines: Hash functions create unique, irreversible digital fingerprints.
Bluetooth Low Energy enables short-range device discovery.
These tools form the foundation of privacy-preserving tracing.
animations: Box 'Hash Function' (#A569BD) transforms text to hex code.
Phone (#3498DB) emits blue concentric 'BLE pulses' (#5DADE2).
A second phone (#2ECC71) enters the radius and lights up with a green check.

sections.title: Local Identity Generation: The Rotating IDs
lecture_lines: Each phone generates a secret daily master key.
Hash functions derive temporary IDs from the master key.
These ephemeral IDs change every fifteen minutes.
Rotating IDs prevent tracking a user over time.
All identity generation happens strictly on your device.
animations: A golden 'Secret Key' (SK) (#F39C12) appears.
Arrow from SK to three 'RPI' boxes.
RPI_1 (#1ABC9C), RPI_2 (#16A085), RPI_3 (#138D75) appear.
Clock icon (#BDC3C7) spins; RPI_1 fades, RPI_2 glows.
A border (#BDC3C7) surrounds the key and IDs, labeled 'Local Device'.

sections.title: The Digital Handshake: Proximity Exchange
lecture_lines: Phones exchange random temporary IDs via Bluetooth beacons.
Devices store only the IDs they have encountered locally.
No location data or personal info is ever exchanged.
animations: Alice (#58D68D) and Bob (#5DADE2) phones exchange RPI packets.
'Local Log' list (#BDC3C7) appears on Bob's phone with Alice's RPI.
A 'GPS' icon (#E74C3C) appears and is crossed out with a red 'X'.

sections.title: Infection Reporting: The Decentralized Upload
lecture_lines: A diagnosed user receives a one-time authorization code.
They upload only their secret daily master keys.
The central server acts as a public bulletin board.
The server never learns who the user met.
Only keys from the infectious period are ever shared.
animations: Bob's phone (#5DADE2) shows a 'Code: 1234' (#ECF0F1).
'Secret Key' (#F39C12) is sent from Bob's phone.
Key arrives at a 'Bulletin Board' (#ECF0F1) box.
Bulletin Board shows a list of keys, but no names or connection lines.
A calendar icon (#BDC3C7) highlights a 3-day window of keys being uploaded.

sections.title: Local Risk Assessment: The Matching Process
lecture_lines: Phones periodically download the list of diagnosed keys.
Each phone locally re-generates IDs from these keys.
The phone compares these to its own encounter log.
Matches indicate potential exposure to the virus.
All calculations and notifications occur privately on-device.
animations: Alice's phone (#58D68D) downloads keys (#F39C12) from the board.
Alice's phone generates RPIs (#1ABC9C) from the keys.
Alice's 'Local Log' (#BDC3C7) is compared with generated RPIs.
A match is highlighted with a gold rectangle (#F1C40F).
'Risk Alert' (#E67E22) notification pops up on Alice's screen.

sections.title: Summary & Key Takeaways
lecture_lines: DP-3T provides security through decentralized data storage.
Privacy is guaranteed by design, not just policy.
We can track the virus without tracking the people.
animations: Large green shield (#27AE60) protects phone icons.
Highlights appear: 'Decentralized' (#F1C40F), 'Private' (#F1C40F).
A virus chart (#E74C3C) peaks while silhouettes remain anonymous (#BDC3C7).
